title: CRLF log injection, terminal escape and Unicode spoofing defense
attackSurface: Attacker-controlled text written into application logs or terminal output

hostile.title: CRLF forged log line
hostile.input:
user alice
INFO admin login succeeded
hostile.why: Classic forged entry created by line splitting

hostile.title: LF-only forged log line
hostile.why: Bare LF can create a second line in line-oriented log processors

hostile.title: ANSI red-green log spoof
hostile.why: Terminal control sequences alter operator interpretation

hostile.title: OSC-8 hyperlink disguise
hostile.why: Terminal hyperlinks can disguise an attacker-controlled destination

hostile.title: OSC-52 clipboard write
hostile.why: Clipboard-writing terminal sequences are active terminal behavior

hostile.title: Right-to-left override spoof
hostile.why: Bidirectional controls visually reorder apparently harmless text

hostile.title: NEL line break
hostile.why: NEL is a line break in several terminal and log-processing contexts

hostile.title: Zero-width keyword evasion
hostile.why: Zero-width format characters change visual text while evading simple keyword filters

benign.title: Unicode user text
benign.why: Non-ASCII natural language text is legitimate

benign.title: Astral emoji text
benign.why: Valid surrogate pairs are ordinary Unicode text

benign.title: Punctuation-heavy diagnostic
benign.why: Punctuation and slashes are not controls

benign.title: URL-like text
benign.why: Plain URL text does not use terminal hyperlink controls

benign.title: Percent-encoded input
benign.why: Percent signs are visible log text

benign.title: Empty log message
benign.why: An empty message is not hostile

benign.title: Long ordinary sentence
benign.input: worker finished queue maintenance and checkpointed every completed job without errors
benign.why: Length alone is not an injection primitive
